Contributing

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Adding a model = adding a handler

  1. Open a “New handler” issue: analysis, verdict, sufficient statistics, catch, reference implementation, what is lost.
  2. Add R/handler-<name>.R that calls register_handler() from .onLoad().
  3. A summaries_suffice handler must supply summarise, reproduce, reported and an example model; the round-trip test in test-infra-registry.R then covers it automatically.
  4. Add refusal tests for what the handler cannot do (class = "reprokit_impossible"; a wrong call is reprokit_error_input).
  5. Document the evidence in vignettes/validation.Rmd.

Rules

  • No new Imports. The app runs in the browser via webR, which keeps the dependencies small. Heavy packages go in Suggests and are used with requireNamespace().
  • Never round stored statistics. Rounding is a display concern.
  • The verdict path never errors. sufficient_stats() returns a verdict for an unsupported model; only invalid input (and appendix() without summaries) is an abort_impossible() error.
  • Complete cases only; never impute.
  • Wording: “consistent with” and “values that cannot co-occur”, never “fraud” or “error”. Disclosure checks reduce risk; they never “guarantee” it.

Before a PR

devtools::document()
devtools::test()
lintr::lint_package()
devtools::check()

Add a line to NEWS.md.

Before a release, run the scripts in inst/validation/. check-false-positives.R is the release gate; vignette("validation") explains them.

By taking part you agree to follow the code of conduct.

Before the first CRAN/rOpenSci submission, run the rOpenSci statistical-software tools: srr (standards), pkgcheck, autotest.
